title: South Carolina AI Laws

reading.body:
South Carolina's only AI-related law is a commemorative week, not a rule that governs anyone.

The state has enacted one AI-related law, H5085, passed February 4, 2026. It declares March 30 to April 2, 2026 as AI Week and encourages citizens to learn more about artificial intelligence. It imposes no obligation on developers, deployers, or state agencies.

That distinction matters for AI infrastructure. A state that has passed only a recognition week has no statutory mechanism for siting data centers, allocating power, or conditioning grid interconnection on AI load. The binding constraints on AI scaling are buildings and power, and those are governed by utility commissions, siting boards, and local ordinances, none of which this data covers.

The data covers one enacted law and nothing else. It does not show pending bills, executive orders, utility proceedings, or local rules, so it cannot establish that South Carolina is doing nothing on AI. It establishes only that the enacted-law record contains one item, and that item is ceremonial.

How this page is kept
